title: Amethyst aura
caption: Twilight and the Milky Way over the Atacama Desert, Chile
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A red glow lingers behind the mountains where the Sun sits low, fading upward into a blue-black sky. Above the desert, the Milky Way spreads out richly, its stars appearing in purple tones. Babak Tafreshi photographed this night sky over Chile's Atacama Desert.

The scene captures a moment of overlap between day and night. Sunlight scattered by the atmosphere still colors the horizon, while higher up the sky has already darkened enough for the band of our galaxy to show through, so both kinds of light appear in one photograph.
The Milky Way is our home galaxy seen from inside its flat disc. Its countless distant stars, too faint to pick out one by one, merge into a soft, glowing band that stretches above the desert.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera in the Atacama Desert. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way appears brighter and more colorful than it would to someone standing in the desert at dusk.

explore: Photographers often work in this brief window between sunset and full darkness, when a sky still holding a trace of color can be combined with the first stars and the glow of the Milky Way.
alt: A red glow behind dark mountains fading into a blue-black sky, with the Milky Way's stars in purple tones above the desert.
